_note: COMP follow-up grid, written 2026-09-18 from docs/comp-model-2026-09-18.md. Normal signal set (`make signals-normal`). Block 1 only: 3BEQ off, WAH off, DST off, every Block 2 slot off; Output Level at the campaign's fixed ~55% mark; the reference every row is divided by is captures/AX30G_BYPASS_IN-LIN.wav. Pass 1 (capture/grids/comp.json, 11 rows) settled the FORM: 1/gain = a + b*E, E the peak envelope of the input, a set by Sensitivity, b = B(Level) - a/Q. What it could NOT settle is listed row by row below.
_note_axes:
Four things are under-determined and each has its own block of rows:
  (1) THE LAW BELOW -40 dBFS. The 5 s ramp starts at -40 dBFS, so `a` -- the reciprocal of the block's MAXIMUM gain -- is an extrapolation, and at Sensitivity 50 it extrapolates to +34 dB where the silence-floor evidence suggests something nearer +19 dB. The rows marked SEND -30 dB are ordinary normal-set captures taken with the interface send 30 dB below the calibrated level, so the same ramp covers -70 to -30 dBFS instead of -40 to 0; analysis/align.py measures the send level per capture and analysis/comp2.py de-scales by it, so nothing else changes. Take the matching BYPASS capture at the same send level first.
  (2) THE ATTACK LAW. Only 0, 25 and 50 were captured and 0 and 25 came out 2.7 and 2.8 ms against 50's 9.6 ms, so the control does almost nothing over its bottom half and everything over its top half -- or the detector's own time constant is a floor that 0 and 25 both sit on. Eight intermediate points decide it.
  (3) THE LEVEL LAW. Three points: 0 (a mute), 25 and 50. Everything between is a guess, and the two rows that measure Level's effect on b disagree (Level 25->50 divides b by 2.40 at Sensitivity 40 and by 1.93 at Sensitivity 50) -- so the Level rows are repeated at a second Sensitivity.
  (4) THE SENSITIVITY LAW. Five points (0, 10, 25, 40, 50) and `a` falls off a cliff between 40 and 50 (0.354 -> 0.020). Six intermediate points.

_note: (1) LOW LEVEL, SEND -30 dB. Repeat of the pass-1 centre row with the send 30 dB down, so the ramp runs -70 to -30 dBFS and the two steady sines land at -50 and -70. This is the row that measures the maximum gain directly instead of extrapolating to it. Capture AX30G_BYPASS at the same send level in the same sitting.

(1) LOW LEVEL, SEND -30 dB. Sensitivity 50 is where the extrapolation is worst: the two-parameter law says the gain keeps climbing to +34 dB below -50 dBFS, the noise floor says it flattens nearer +19 dB. If it flattens, the model needs a maximum-gain clamp or a detector floor and this row measures which.

(1) LOW LEVEL, SEND -30 dB. Sensitivity 25: the middle of the range, where the extrapolation is mild. If this row nulls on the pass-1 model and the Sensitivity 50 row does not, the clamp is real and sits high.

(1) LOW LEVEL, SEND -30 dB. Sensitivity 0, the floor of the Sensitivity axis: with a = 1.034 the law says the gain never exceeds -0.3 dB, so this row should null on the pass-1 model with nothing added. It is the control that says the reduced send itself changes nothing.
(2) ATTACK axis at Sensitivity 40 / Level 25 -- read from the gain trajectory inside the 60 ms bursts. Attack 5.
(2) ATTACK axis, upper half -- this is where all of the control's effect lives, so these four rows carry the law.
(2) ATTACK at a second Sensitivity: the pass-1 model assumes the attack law does not depend on Sensitivity, and this row and the next test that at the two ends of the Attack range.

(3) LEVEL axis at Sensitivity 40 / Attack 25. Level moves b (the output ceiling) and leaves a (the maximum gain) alone -- 25 -> 50 raised the ceiling 7.59 dB and changed a by 0.22 dB -- which is not what an output makeup gain does, so the shape of this axis matters. Level 5.

(3) LEVEL 1: one step above the mute. If Level is a table with entry 0 forced to zero, this row says how big the first real step is; if Level is a linear amplitude scaling, this row is 28 dB below Level 25.

(3) LEVEL axis repeated at Sensitivity 25 / Attack 25 -- three points, enough to say whether B(Level) is the same curve at every Sensitivity. Pass 1's two Level-50 rows disagreed about the 25 -> 50 ratio (2.40 at Sensitivity 40, 1.93 at Sensitivity 50), but the Sensitivity 50 one was also the Attack 0 corner row and fitted 10x worse than the rest, so this settles it on clean rows.

(4) SENSITIVITY axis at Level 25 / Attack 25, filling in between pass 1's 0/10/25/40/50. `a` is 0.354 at 40 and 0.020 at 50, so the top of the axis is where the law is doing something violent and where the four rows 42/45/47/50 matter most.
